title: Discovering Authenticity: Unmasking the Layers
summary: A 4:32 music-framed monologue arguing that every interview contains lies because judgment makes people exaggerate and hide details. School/job/admissions/supermarket audiences introduce self-presentation; crude butt-cheek-taping and getting-caught-DUI claims exemplify omitted details. Television, film, documentaries and reality shows become a broader fiction critique. A Bill Murray interview represents the desire for honesty. The speaker cites thousands of conversations from hitchhiking, travel, art and music, seeking moments when guards/masks/facades drop. He repeatedly asks why people lie, answers that he wants to be liked, calls himself self-destructive and full of self-hatred, says he pushes away love, and explores family/friend/enemy behavior. A masked bathroom white-lie joke leads to self-implication: even believing one should never lie, he still does. The close theorizes that rejection fear and desire for love/acceptance can produce lying, cheating, stealing, hurt and attachment to pain/misery, while he wants out. Every absolute, crude example, mask and self-accusation remains. The opening phrase stays unclear and the short music lyric remains separate. No act/crime, diagnosis, universal causal model, song or voice is invented.
